title: Fed holds, two vote to hike: what it means for gold, oil and yields
summary: The Fed kept rates at 3.75%–4.00% with two dissents for a hike. Gold slips towards $4,040, oil eases on renewed US–Iran contacts, and the 10-year yield sits above 5% ahead of the ECB, US GDP and PCE.
coverAlt: Market Desk cover: gold and WTI over 30 sessions with key market levels
html:
What happened

The Federal Reserve kept its policy rate at 3.75%–4.00% on Wednesday, but the vote was 10–2: Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favour of a 25-basis-point hike. Two hawkish dissents at a hold is an unusual signal, and futures pricing moved towards a hike at the December meeting. Chair Kevin Warsh said upcoming data will decide the next step and that the November 3 midterm elections played no role.

US equities still closed slightly higher: the S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98, the Nasdaq Composite 0.27% and the Dow 0.19%. After the bell, Microsoft beat expectations on Azure while Alphabet fell on a revenue miss — a reminder that the AI trade is now being judged company by company. The US 10-year yield closed above 5% (about 5.04%).

Gold: rates versus geopolitics

Gold dipped to about $4,035 straight after the decision, then recovered towards $4,057 late in US trading. This morning COMEX gold futures trade near $4,038 (−0.3%). The metal is down about 3.5% over the past month and below its 20-day average, after peaking near $4,700 in late August.

What it could mean: a Fed that is openly debating hikes raises the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset, and 10-year yields above 5% add to that pressure. Against it, the war involving Iran and attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure keep safe-haven demand alive. Levels cited by analysts this week: support around $4,025–4,035 and $3,980–4,000, resistance around $4,101–4,110. Today's US GDP and PCE inflation data are the next test: hot inflation would strengthen the case for a December hike, while softer numbers would ease pressure on gold.

Oil: diplomacy against missiles

Crude gave back part of Wednesday's gain. Brent trades around $114 (about −1%) and WTI around $101 (−1.4% to −1.8%) after reports that Vice President JD Vance wrote to Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei to restart peace talks, and that Qatari mediators have put a new draft deal to Tehran. The downside is limited by Houthi claims of a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (not confirmed by Saudi authorities) and by reports that Washington could resume military action after November 3. US crude inventories fell 1.9 million barrels last week while gasoline stocks rose 3.9 million.

What it could mean: oil is trading headlines in both directions, so volatility is likely to stay high into the midterms. Sustained crude above $100 feeds into inflation expectations — one more reason the Fed's hawks are not backing down. UBS now expects Brent to stay near $110 into year-end.

Rates and currencies

The 10-year yield added about 5 basis points to 5.04%. The dollar index holds near 102.2 (+0.6% over five sessions). EUR/USD trades near 1.114 ahead of the ECB, and USD/JPY near 157.9 ahead of the Bank of Japan. In Asia and Europe this morning, the Nikkei 225 gained about 1.1% and the DAX about 0.7%.
